SLOOS-informed modification:
- Policy stance and market functioning: The Fed keeps the funds rate at 0–0.25% and continues Treasury/MBS purchases, reinforcing accommodative market conditions and the flow-based backstop to credit markets.
- Bank lending supply and demand (SLOOS, Q3 2020): Banks broadly tightened lending standards for C&I loans to firms of all sizes and for CRE; many also tightened for consumer credit (credit cards, autos). C&I loan demand weakened, while mortgage demand was strong amid low rates but met with tighter underwriting. Tightening was driven by deteriorating or uncertain credit quality, reduced risk tolerance, and pandemic-related uncertainty; forbearance policies and potential loss recognition also weighed on supply.
- Implications for the outlook: Despite easy market-based financial conditions, the bank credit channel remains restrictive, particularly for SMEs and CRE, which could constrain investment and employment if the pandemic worsens. This corroborates the statement’s emphasis on virus-driven risks and tempers the otherwise positive impact of forward guidance and asset purchases.

Net tone: Slightly more negative than an FSR-only read, given widespread tightening and soft business loan demand in SLOOS.
